name: Tiimo
target_user: Adults and students who want visual time blocking and neurodivergent-friendly planning
core_promise: Reduce mental load and help users follow through with a visual plan
main_features: AI co-planner; visual schedule; drag-and-drop tasks; reminders; Apple Watch support
strengths: Strong accessibility framing; visual structure; flexible schedule view
weaknesses: Android instability; notification and sync issues; premium gating; still planner-centric
user_praise: Visual scheduling can feel life-changing and flexible routines help when plans change
user_hate: Crashes; silent notifications; login/calendar sync problems; premium features feel hidden or paywalled
pricing_or_friction: Free with in-app purchases; App Store currently shows Monthly Pro $12 and Yearly Pro $54
gap_unserved: Still assumes the user can pre-plan and then return to the plan; weak support for interruption recovery and restart friction

name: Structured
target_user: Users who want a clean daily timeline and drag/drop day planning
core_promise: Turn a chaotic day into a clear visual timeline
main_features: Timeline planner; recurring tasks; optional AI; imports from calendar/reminders on some platforms
strengths: Excellent simplicity; attractive UI; easy day reshuffling
weaknesses: Core Pro features vary by platform; reminder discoverability issues; lag; Android/web parity gaps
user_praise: Users love sliding their day around and seeing tasks visually
user_hate: Essential features behind Pro; reminders hard to find or enable; slowness and feature gaps
pricing_or_friction: Free with optional Pro; official help says monthly, yearly, or lifetime purchase with region-based pricing
gap_unserved: Great for seeing the day, not for reconstructing lost context after interruptions

name: Inflow
target_user: Adults seeking ADHD education, structure, and supportive coaching content
core_promise: Provide ADHD-friendly education, coaching, and symptom-management support
main_features: Short modules; coaching/community features; reminders; journaling; AI/chat elements
strengths: Empathetic tone; supportive framing; engaging content; some users like coworking/coaching
weaknesses: High price; bugs and crashes; reminders criticized; generic content; removed features damaged trust
user_praise: Helpful modules and an understanding tone can make users feel seen
user_hate: Freezes; missing reminders; exploitative pricing feel; coaching changes; too much self-help and not enough action
pricing_or_friction: Official FAQ lists $199/year or $47.99/month after a 7-day free trial
gap_unserved: Better at psychoeducation than in-the-moment rescue when a user is stuck or has lost the thread

name: Goblin Tools
target_user: Neurodivergent users who need help decomposing tasks or interpreting communication
core_promise: Turn overwhelming tasks and messy thoughts into actionable steps
main_features: Magic ToDo; estimator; compiler; tone tools; language tools
strengths: Very strong value signal; low-cost app plus free web; excellent task breakdown utility
weaknesses: Limited reminders/integrations/widgets; app instability; not built for persistent task context
user_praise: Users love how well it breaks down tasks and reduces overwhelm
user_hate: Freezing; disappearing tasks; poor task ordering; missing notifications and recurring support
pricing_or_friction: Official site says app purchases keep the free website alive; App Store currently lists $2.99 iOS purchase
gap_unserved: Helps define the steps, but does not preserve live context or restart interrupted work later

name: Focusmate
target_user: People who focus better with another person present
core_promise: Use virtual coworking to overcome procrastination and stay accountable
main_features: Scheduled focus sessions; partner matching; recurring sessions
strengths: Strong proof that accountability and co-working can help initiate work
weaknesses: Requires session setup; depends on partner availability and etiquette; social pressure can be a barrier
user_praise: Often described as a game changer for procrastination and focus
user_hate: No partner available; continuity is weak; some users want less social pressure and more regularity
pricing_or_friction: Official pricing is free for 3 sessions per week; Plus is $8/month billed annually or $12/month billed monthly
gap_unserved: Great during a session, but weak as asynchronous rescue when a user gets interrupted alone

name: Motion
target_user: Busy professionals and students who want task auto-scheduling
core_promise: Automatically schedule and re-prioritize work around deadlines and calendar events
main_features: AI task planner; calendar; meetings; docs; notes; mobile and desktop apps
strengths: Auto-rescheduling can surface forgotten work and reduce manual calendar maintenance
weaknesses: Cluttered UI; setup burden; performance complaints; expensive; still does not guarantee follow-through
user_praise: Users like calendar sync and the way lower-priority tasks still resurface
user_hate: Buggy updates; costly; over-complex; tasks can still be ignored even when scheduled
pricing_or_friction: Official pricing page currently shows Pro AI at $19/seat/month and Business AI at $29/seat/month with annual savings messaging visible
gap_unserved: Good for scheduling, weak for the moment after interruption when a user needs state restoration and a restart cue

name: Finch
target_user: Users who want motivation, journaling, and emotionally warm self-care structure
core_promise: Make self-care feel rewarding, lightweight, and fun
main_features: Virtual pet; quick exercises; goals; journaling; widgets; reminders
strengths: Excellent warmth and retention hooks; strong free tier; motivational design
weaknesses: More self-care than executive-function rescue; occasional bugs; price variability confuses some users
user_praise: Cute design and reinforcement make routines feel easier to maintain
user_hate: Pricing confusion; streak bugs; support complaints; less useful for cognitively heavy work
pricing_or_friction: Free with in-app purchases; App Store currently shows multiple Finch Plus price points
gap_unserved: Helpful for gentle consistency, but not designed to recover task context after distraction
